title: SECOND PROPERTY TAX PAYMENT DUE TOMORROW
full_story:
The second installment of the 2025 payable 2026 Real Estate Tax Bill is due tomorrow.  If you have questions about your tax bill, please feel free to call the Treasurer’s office.  If you cannot get through, please leave a message.  Phone 618-665-3727.

Payment can be made to the Clay County Treasurer using any of the following options, by mail send your check with the payment stub to the Clay County Treasurer PO Box 88 Louisville, IL 62858.  Mailed payments must be postmarked on or before the due date to avoid penalty.

At the treasurer’s office in the Clay County Courthouse where they accept cash, check, cashier’s check, or money order.  Bring your entire bill if you want it stamped to show proof of payment.  Office hours are 8:00 am to 4:00 pm Monday through Friday but closed on national holidays.

Online by credit/debit card: Go to www.govpaynow.com PLC #a00082.

Or by drop box at the north entrance of the Clay County Courthouse.  Please include payment stub.

title: XENIA SHED FIRE
full_story:
A Wednesday afternoon shed fire near Xenia left one person with minor injuries and required firefighters to return hours later to put out a rekindle.

Units from the Xenia Fire Protection District were called out around 3:14 Wednesday afternoon to the 1,300 block of Oak Mound Lane.  Firefighters arrived to find a 12-by-20-foot shed fully engulfed in flames, with a nearby garage threatened by the heat.

Eleven firefighters with two engines and a tanker worked for just under two hours to protect the garage and extinguish the blaze.  The shed is considered a total loss.

The homeowner suffered minor injuries and was taken to a local hospital by Clay County Ambulance.  Clay County Electric Cooperative also assisted at the scene.

Crews were called back to the property at 8:14 Wednesday night after a wood pile inside the destroyed shed rekindled.  The cause of the original fire remains undetermined.

title: FLORA SCHOOL BOARD
full_story:
The Flora Community Unit School District #35 Board of Education approved its tentative tax levy, honored standout students and staff, and finalized several basketball coaching hires during its regular meeting last night.

Gathering at the Administration Office, board members voted to approve the tentative tax levy as presented.  During his report, Superintendent Joel Hackney shared an update on the district’s strategic planning goals and expressed appreciation to everyone who helped make the November 10th Veterans Day breakfast a major success.

The board also took time to celebrate recent achievements across the district, recognizing the Floyd Henson Junior High faculty and staff for earning an “exemplary” designation for the third consecutive year, alongside the girls’ tennis team and state qualifiers for their successful season.

In personnel action, the board approved three coaching positions for the 2026-2027 boys’ basketball season, Loren Holloway was approved as a high school volunteer assistant coach.  Stephen Smith was hired as 6th Grade head coach, with Jim Earleywine approved as a volunteer assistant.

Additionally, the board hired Khadijah Thomas as a district custodian effective November 23rd and acknowledged Family and Medical Leave Act leave for Kelsey Cox running from approximately March 2nd through April 27th.

title: ACCIDENT DETAILS
full_story:
Authorities have released additional details regarding a two-vehicle collision northeast of Salem on Monday morning that left both drivers hospitalized via air medical transport.

According to the Marion County Sheriff’s Department, the crash occurred at approximately 10:45 am at the intersection of Charleston and Brubaker Roads.

Preliminary investigation indicates that 51-year-old Jacklyn Gray, of Centralia, pulled away from a stop sign on Charleston Road directly into the path of a westbound vehicle traveling on Brubaker Road.  The westbound vehicle was driven by 54-year-old Ronald Hamilton, of Louisville.

Both Gray and Hamilton sustained injuries serious enough to require airlifting from the scene for medical treatment.

A passenger in Hamilton’s vehicle, a 17-year-old female juvenile, was also injured in the collision.  She was transported to Salem Township Hospital for treatment.

The Kinmundy-Alma Fire Protection District and United Medical Response assisted Marion County deputies at the crash site.  No further details regarding the conditions of those involved or potential citations have been released.

title: IECC BOARD MEETING
full_story:
The Illinois Eastern Community Colleges Board of Trustees met on Tuesday at Wabash Valley College in Mount Carmel, taking action on tax levies, potential bond issuances, and upcoming academic and athletic programs.

Trustees approved an estimated tax levy of just over 9.5 million dollars for calendar year 2026.  Because that represents a 6.2% increase over last year, exceeding the 5% state threshold, a Truth in Taxation hearing is scheduled for December 8th at Frontier Community College.

The Board also called for a public hearing regarding the proposed issuance of $4.85 million dollars in Working Cash Fund Bonds and $4.5 million dollars in Protection, Health, and Safety Bonds.  Trustees selected Stifel as the underwriter for the proposed bond sales.

In program updates, the Board backed Chancellor Taylor’s recommendation to complete a comprehensive financial and operational review before moving forward with proposed men’s and women’s soccer programs at Olney Central College.  Those findings are expected in the spring of 2027.  Trustees also agreed to hold off on additional spending for a proposed welding lab conversion at Frontier Community College pending further evaluation.

In other business, the Board recognized Doctor Matt Fowler for 27 years of service to the district.  Approved the purchase of a mini excavator from Bobcat of Effingham for just over $56,000.  Hired Logan Durham as Student Services Specialist at Wabash Valley College and Max McVicker as Enterprise Systems Administrator.

The Board of Trustees will meet next on Tuesday, December 8th, at 5 pm at Frontier Community College in Fairfield, following a morning board retreat.

title: BLOOD DRIVES
full_story:
Clay County residents have an upcoming opportunity to help save lives before the Thanksgiving Holiday.

The American Red Cross is teaming up with the Flora Chamber Of Commerce and Flora Odd Fellows Lodge number 151 for a pre-Thanksgiving blood drive.

The drive will be held Wednesday, from 1:00 to 5:00 pm at the Flora Odd Fellows Lodge, located at 231 East North Avenue in Flora.

Organizers note that the winter holidays often bring a drop in donations, making local drives essential for maintaining area blood supplies.  As an added incentive, those who come out to give blood on Wednesday will receive an exclusive American Red Cross and Wheel Of Fortune mug, while supplies last.

To donate, individuals must be at least 17 years old, weigh at least 110 pounds, and be in generally good health.  Donors are asked to bring a blood donor card, driver’s license, or two other forms of identification.

Appointments can be made using the Red Cross Blood Donor App, by visiting RedCrossBlood.org, by calling 1-800-RED CROSS or by enabling the Blood Donor Skill on Alexa Echo devices.  Donors can use RapidPass online on the day of their appointment to complete pre-donation reading and health history questionnaires before arriving.

There will be a Blood Drive on Tuesday, December 1st from Noon to 6 pm at the Blue Point Free Will Baptist Church in the Link Gymnasium.  The next Blood Drive at the Flora Church of the Nazarene will be on Thursday, December 10th from Noon to 5 pm.

title: WHEAT BOARD ELECTION RESULTS
full_story:
The Illinois Department of Agriculture announced results of the October 28th, Illinois Wheat Development Board election Wednesday.

This election filled three statewide at-large board member positions and two of the six district board member positions on the Illinois Wheat Development Board.

“Congratulations and a big thank you to those being elected to the Illinois Wheat Development Board,” said Jerry Costello II, Director of the Illinois Department of Agriculture.  “I am confident this group will work hard to build a strong and sustainable future for Illinois’ wheat industry.”

The Illinois Wheat Development Board will oversee the check-off dollars derived from assessments levied at the first point of sale.  State law limits the total assessment levied up to 1.5 cents per bushel of wheat.  The program that was adopted by referendum in April 2025 sets the assessment at 1.5 cents per bushel.

Winning the District VI seat was Jamie Harvel, of Clay County, district VI represents Clay, Alexander, Edwards, Gallatin, Hamilton, Hardin, Johnson, Massac, Pope, Pulaski, Saline, Union, Wabash, Wayne, White, Williamson counties.  Winning the Statewide Illinois Wheat Development Board At-Large Board Member seat was Brandon Warren, of Wayne County.  Winning the District III seat was Rob Holscher, from Crawford County, he will represent Champaign, Clark, Coles, Crawford, Cumberland, Douglas, Edgar, Effingham, Fayette, Jasper, Lawrence, Marion, Moultrie, Richland, Shelby, Vermilion counties.

For more information, call the Illinois Department of Agriculture at (217) 524-1083 or the Illinois Wheat Association at (309) 557-3619.
